sentences.translation: There is a shrimp in it.
A child has come out quietly.
The eyes of the shrimp are big.
The child is a little bit stuck.
The child is going by the sardines.
The shrimp are just looking at the children.
The child puts his hand around the comb of a shrimp.
The child sits on the dirt.
The child looks at the shrimp eyes.
"What are you thinking today, Mr. Ushi?"
The shrimp looks slightly toward the mountain.
"Oh, you were looking at the mountain?"
The children also look at the mountains.
I'll give you a little bit of tail.
"Do you want to know the river?" asked the child.
A little bit of a river.
"I wonder if you're coming," said the child.
I want to be on the dirt.
The child will pick up the chopsticks again.
The shrimps are very hard to beat.
The child sits in the soil again.
The sardines are swooping at the tail.
"Here, I am wide, and look at the mountains, and come across the river."
She will look at her children again.
"I may as well have such a day."
I'm a little bit nervous about my children.
"I'll come back tomorrow," the child said.
Children are in the wrong direction.
It's a little bit, and it's pretending.
The raven is still standing wide.
The child is a little bit soft.
The Ushi is still in the open.
With big eyes, look at the mountains, and cross the river.
It was a nice day today.
